title: The article scroll indicator does not reflect position in the document
acceptance: Scrolling a long article shows an indicator that reflects true position in the whole document, not in the realised subset
It is correct on a very long document — Frankenstein-scale, once T-0027 lands the untruncated text
It stays correct after the reader's text size changes
It does not force every block to lay out up front; the lazy rendering that makes long documents usable is preserved
notes: User report 2026-08-25: 'the scrollbar on the articles does not work'. Diagnosis: there is no .scrollIndicators(.hidden) anywhere — the cause is structural. ReaderView wraps a LazyVStack in a ScrollView, so the ScrollView only knows the height of blocks that have been realised. The indicator therefore sizes and positions itself against a content height that grows as you scroll, which is exactly the symptom. This is a direct consequence of the per-block architecture kept at T-0002; the lazy rendering is what makes an 80,000-word document usable, so the fix must not trade it away. Likely answer is an estimated total height from block count and type, or a purpose-built reading-progress indicator rather than relying on the system scrollbar. Depends on T-0022 to avoid colliding on ArticleBlockView.
